Fourier series operators¶

Back to Operators

A Fourier series writes a function on an interval as a sum of sines and cosines. The operators in operators::fourier build the coefficients and the partial sums as Functions: each coefficient is a definite integral of the function against a trigonometric function, built through the integral operator, and each series is the sum of those coefficients times the matching waves. As elsewhere, applying an operator evaluates nothing; the result is a formula that waits for values.

Operator

Result for f on [a, b]

cosine_coefficients(x, a, b, n)

A_k = 2/(b−a) ∫ f cos(kπ(x−a)/(b−a)) dx, k = 0..n−1, a vector Function

sine_coefficients(x, a, b, n)

B_k = 2/(b−a) ∫ f sin(kπ(x−a)/(b−a)) dx, k = 1..n

cosine_series(x, a, b, n)

A₀/2 + Σ A_k cos(kπ(x−a)/(b−a)), the even extension

sine_series(x, a, b, n)

Σ B_k sin(kπ(x−a)/(b−a)), the odd extension

coefficients(x, L, n), series(x, L, n)

the full trigonometric series on [−L, L]: the cosine series of the even part plus the sine series of the odd part

Both half-range forms also take a support [from, to] inside [a, b]: the integral then runs over the support only, which is how a payoff that vanishes on part of the interval is expanded (the cosine expansion method of option pricing uses exactly this).

operators::Operator operators::fourier::cosine_coefficients(std::string_view variable, double lower, double upper, std::int64_t terms);
operators::Operator operators::fourier::cosine_coefficients(std::string_view variable, double lower, double upper, std::int64_t terms, double support_lower, double support_upper);
operators::Operator operators::fourier::sine_coefficients(std::string_view variable, double lower, double upper, std::int64_t terms);
operators::Operator operators::fourier::cosine_series(std::string_view variable, double lower, double upper, std::int64_t terms);
operators::Operator operators::fourier::sine_series(std::string_view variable, double lower, double upper, std::int64_t terms);
operators::Operator operators::fourier::coefficients(std::string_view variable, double half_period, std::int64_t terms);
operators::Operator operators::fourier::series(std::string_view variable, double half_period, std::int64_t terms);

Coefficients with a closed form¶

For f(x) = x on [0, π] the sine coefficients are B_k = 2(−1)^{k+1}/k and the cosine coefficients are A₀ = π and A_k = −4/(πk²) for odd k, zero for even k. The operators recover them from the integral, and the sine series converges to x away from the end x = π, where its odd extension jumps.

#include <pluss/ma.h>
#include <pluss/tils/aux/output.h>

namespace math = pluss::math;
namespace operators = pluss::operators;
namespace fourier = pluss::operators::fourier;
using namespace pluss::tils;

int main() {
  OutputEngine out;
  out.print_defaults(PrintOptions{}.fixed(6));
  const double pi = std::acos(-1.0);
  const math::Function identity = math::function({"x"}, [](math::Function x) { return x; });

  // staged: build the operators once, apply them to the same function
  const operators::Operator sine = fourier::sine_coefficients("x", 0.0, pi, 6);
  const operators::Operator cosine = fourier::cosine_coefficients("x", 0.0, pi, 6);
  out.writeln("B_1..B_6  ", sine(identity)().pull<double>());
  out.writeln("closed    ", std::vector<double>{2.0, -1.0, 2.0 / 3, -0.5, 0.4, -1.0 / 3});
  out.writeln("A_0..A_5  ", cosine(identity)().pull<double>());
  out.writeln("closed    ", std::vector<double>{pi, -4.0 / pi, 0.0, -4.0 / (9 * pi), 0.0, -4.0 / (25 * pi)});

  // compact: partial sums are Functions of x
  for (const std::int64_t terms : {2, 8, 32})
    out.writeln("sine series, ", terms, " terms   ", fourier::sine_series("x", 0.0, pi, terms)(identity)({pluss::make_series(1.0)}).item<double>());
}

Output

B_1..B_6   [2.000000, -1.000000, 0.666667, -0.500000, 0.400000, -0.333333]
closed     [2.000000, -1.000000, 0.666667, -0.500000, 0.400000, -0.333333]
A_0..A_5   [3.141593, -1.273240, -0.000000, -0.141471, -0.000000, -0.050930]
closed     [3.141593, -1.273240, 0.000000, -0.141471, 0.000000, -0.050930]
sine series,  2  terms    0.773645
sine series,  8  terms    0.896065
sine series,  32  terms    0.968884

The full series, and Parseval¶

On [−π, π] the odd function x has only sine terms, and the even function x² only cosine terms. The coefficients operator returns [a₀ … a_{n−1}, b₁ … b_{n−1}], so the two cases show up as zero blocks. Parseval’s identity ties the coefficients to the energy of the function, (1/π) ∫ f² dx = a₀²/2 + Σ (a_k² + b_k²); the program compares the two sides for x², whose energy is 2π⁴/5·1/π.

#include <pluss/ma.h>
#include <pluss/tils/aux/output.h>

namespace math = pluss::math;
namespace fourier = pluss::operators::fourier;
using namespace pluss::tils;

int main() {
  OutputEngine out;
  out.print_defaults(PrintOptions{}.fixed(6));
  const double pi = std::acos(-1.0);
  const math::Function odd = math::function({"x"}, [](math::Function x) { return x; });
  const math::Function even = math::function({"x"}, [](math::Function x) { return x * x; });

  const std::vector<double> c = fourier::coefficients("x", pi, 8)(even)().pull<double>();  // a_0..a_7, b_1..b_7
  out.writeln("x   : ", fourier::coefficients("x", pi, 8)(odd)().pull<double>());
  out.writeln("x^2 : ", c);

  double energy = 0.5 * c[0] * c[0];
  for (std::size_t k = 1; k < c.size(); ++k) energy += c[k] * c[k];
  out.writeln("Parseval: ", energy, "   (1/pi) int x^4 = ", 2.0 * std::pow(pi, 4) / 5.0);
  out.writeln("series(2) = ", fourier::series("x", pi, 8)(even)({pluss::make_series(2.0)}).item<double>(), "   x^2 = 4");
}

Output

x   :  [-0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 2.000000, -1.000000, 0.666667, -0.500000, 0.400000, -0.333333, 0.285714]
x^2 :  [6.579736, -4.000000, 1.000000, -0.444444, 0.250000, -0.160000, 0.111111, -0.081633, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000, 0.000000]
Parseval:  38.951105    (1/pi) int x^4 =  38.963636
series(2) =  4.054545    x^2 = 4

What can be saved¶

The six operators hold names and numbers and save with math::io::save (Saving and loading).
